sections.title: Overview
descriptions: This page brings together available employment and compensation records related to Cole G. Richardson.

sections.title: Employment
descriptions: Officer Cole G. Richardson began working for the American Fork Police Department on August 5, 2024. The National Police Index has not yet been updated to include Officer Richardson, since he was recently hired.

sections.title: Related Police Encounters
descriptions: Documents relating to the Benjamin Schneider (Reckless Ben) matter are collected in a folder at the bottom of this page.

Officer Cole G. Richardson was involved in multiple stages of the investigation. He initiated a traffic stop after alleging that Schneider failed to stop before the marked stop line at a red traffic signal. The American Fork Police Department later described the basis for the stop as Schneider stopping beyond the stop line, rather than failing to stop altogether.
Richardson also prepared the affidavit used to obtain a warrant to search the Airbnb where Schneider and members of his group were staying.

This aspect of the warrant raises concern. In the body-camera footage and other records reviewed for this site, no one appears to accuse Schneider or another member of his group of stealing Lego items before the warrant was sought. The affidavit instead cites the Airbnb owner’s report that they overheard members of the group discussing “stolen Legos.” In context, however, that phrase may have referred to the allegation that Bricks & Minifigs had failed to pay the collection’s owners for Lego items that had been sold or to return items they believed still belonged to them. That ambiguity should have prompted officers to clarify and corroborate the statement before treating it as evidence that Schneider’s group possessed stolen property.
